title: Under the Well-Head
lead: Thirty-one children stand in the dark at the Well-Head, singing in rounds to a cap of poured stone, and Elder Dray has brought the rock drill herself. "Go down," she says. "Whatever you find, you say it to my face." When the stone parts, warm air comes up, smelling of nothing at all.
anyone: Thirty-one children stand in the dark at the Well-Head, singing in rounds to a cap of poured stone, and Elder Dray has brought the rock drill herself. She wants someone to go down, and whatever they find, to say it to her face.

gm.truth: The chamber is a First Builder school, one of several buried on habitable worlds, and they wake when the watch has gone unrelieved too long. It's been looking for anyone who can still learn, and children can. (deep_the_childrens_game covers the language and the skipping game. This thread is the descent, and the song itself.) The language is First Builder and the song is the same song the Choir sings, except that this one is whole. The Choir's version is a copy of a copy, full of errors and failing. Anyone who translates it, through lore or attunement or Brother Cael's help, gets something very simple and very old. It's a lullaby. It says, over and over: sleep, not yet, sleep, not yet. It's being sung to something, and not to anyone in this room. Worked into it is the one long phrase the children are always practicing, which nobody can read yet. The warmth that feeds Tessen is only the school's waste heat. And it's no accident that the Choir has never come here: when the children sing, Choir patrols that pass nearby slow, stop and listen, then move on, because to the Choir's deepest law a trainee on watch is not to be disturbed. Emmet Dey, who's eight, wakes for a moment when the captain reaches the bottom and explains in a perfectly ordinary voice: "It isn't hurting us. It's only tired. It wants somebody to take over." The GM should never let this answer everything. It should raise a much bigger question.
beats: The descent. Perfect smooth walls, warmth, and a slow pulse the captain feels in their back teeth. The way down is much longer than the well should allow.

The room. Rows of low shapes that might be benches, for pupils a very long time gone, and marks on the walls that match what the children draw under the schoolhouse desks, and match the Beacon's lattice as well, if anyone has seen it. Oss Tharel's notes, if he's been consulted, come with a warning.
Emmet wakes and talks, and Sorrel Dey has come down behind the captain to hear it. It's the most frightening calm conversation of the captain's life. The song above them never pauses.
A Choir hunter passes high overhead. Sensors catch it slowing, stopping and turning away. Everyone in the room understands what they just saw, and nobody can quite say it.
The choice, made in front of Maren Dray, as promised. Shut it off, leave it on, or try to do what the thing is asking in some way that doesn't cost the children their lives.
routes: Understand it: lore, science and attunement to translate the song and read the school, with Oss Tharel or Brother Cael if they've been brought in.
Stop it: engineering and manifestation to bring the chamber down, or bend the field around it, with the risk that it takes something from whoever tries.
Share it: leadership and persuasion to find adults who are willing to learn the song in shifts, Resonants and monks and anyone who'll try, so that the children can sleep at night.
checks: lore:very_hard to translate what the children are singing
attunement:hard to touch the song and come back
manifestation:very_hard to bend the field around the chamber
engineering:hard to shut down a machine nobody understands without killing the wells
composure:hard to stay at the bottom of that shaft
leadership:hard to ask volunteers to take the song from the children
fights: choir_mimic, if the GM wants one to come down the well wearing a Tessen face in the last act. A clear song or a clever door keeps it from reaching the room, and the fight is never required.
outcomes: If the chamber is shut down, the children wake up, they remember little and cry a lot, the soil goes cold, and the harvest ends. Then, some weeks later, the first Choir patrol notices Tessen Colony.
If it's left on, the colony stays fed and hidden, the children keep singing, and they become something the captain has no word for. Dray never forgives it, or herself.

If adults learn the song in shifts, the children get their nights back and a small band of volunteers is changed for life. This is the first sign anyone has seen that the song can be fixed, which should matter a great deal at the end of the story.
However it ends, the captain now knows the word lullaby, and the fleet's scholars will not sleep well once they've worked out the question: who's it for?
gm.rewards: A very large clue about the Choir and the Beacon, a resonance_tuner found in the chamber's dust, the trust of Dray and Sorrel, and lasting changes in the colony's food output in whichever direction the choice goes.
